_: A declaration to correct rather than a file to fill. Delete what does not apply, change every lifetime that is wrong, and keep the note field as your own record of why. Correcting a proposal surfaces disagreements that a blank file hides.
_audit: Only read by the audit report (--audit). Never invented: a field left empty prints as a field to complete, and the statement is yours to write, date and sign.

accounting.note: Usually the easiest one: legal retention answers it. Ten years in France. Start here, it warms people up.

contracts and legal.note: How long could this document still be produced in a dispute? People underestimate this one badly.

hr and payroll.note: Five years after departure is common, but pension records run for decades. Ask which of the two this is.

health or sensitive personal data.note: If this domain exists at all, it is almost always the one that decides the whole report. Delete it if it does not apply — do not leave it in to look thorough.

customer identity.note: Driven by your retention policy, not by the code. Whoever wrote that policy is the person to ask.

payment references.note: The card token is short-lived; the mandate reference and the transaction trail are not. Ask which one you actually store.

backups.note: The one people get wrong. A backup's lifetime is the MAXIMUM of everything inside it — so it inherits the longest domain above, whatever that is. This is where most red verdicts come from.

secrets and credentials.note: Not 'until we rotate'. A sealed vault copied today is decrypted the day the curve falls, and rotating afterwards does not recover what was already taken.

sessions and tokens.note: Short by design. Worth declaring anyway: it is the domain that proves the tool is not just shouting at everything.

logs and telemetry.note: Usually short, but check what ends up in them. Logs that carry identifiers inherit the lifetime of what they identify.

internal correspondence.note: The forgotten one. Nobody sets a retention policy for email, and it outlives everything.

public content.note: Zero, and saying so matters: it stops the report treating published pages as a confidentiality problem.

code signing or internal certificate aut.note: The only place where a signature is urgent. trust_anchor changes the verdict: a signature that must still verify after the expiry year is prepared years ahead.
